primary_claim: Precursor evaluations for scheming (agentic self-reasoning and agentic theory of mind), designed in May 2024, had only low-to-medium predictive power for later in-context scheming evaluations; the 'easy' precursor versions were somewhat useful as predictors, but the 'hard' versions were neutral or actively misleading.

effect.metric: predictive power of precursor evals for in-context scheming evals

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies the assumption, embedded in frontier safety policies, that precursor evaluations reliably serve as triggers preceding the capabilities they are meant to predict
stated_future_work: Further research into the science of evaluations
Building evaluations that measure the capability of interest directly instead of precursors wherever possible
limitations_stated: This is a research note based on a small suite of evaluations, with analysis less rigorous than the authors' standard for a published paper
Both eval suites likely have flaws, some known when built, some only realized over time
quote: the “easy” versions of our evals are somewhat useful as predictors, but the “hard” versions are neutral or actively misleading.
